summary: Wave of 5xx errors after connection drain during rolling deploy - partial runtime OOMs and API 502s
description: Issue summary: Customers observed an abrupt spike of 502/503 errors and elevated 5xx rates for streaming and short-chat calls immediately following a scheduled rolling deployment in us-east. Impact: Multiple enterprise customers on Dedicated capacity (including NimbusDocs) reported failed requests, higher tail latency, and partial runtime crashes. Initial symptoms indicated connection termination during node drain leading to request retries and downstream overload.
impact: Approximately 8% of requests returned 5xx over a 12 minute window for the us-east pool. Several long-lived streaming sessions dropped mid-stream. No data corruption observed; primary impact is availability and degraded latency for affected tenants.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a rolling deploy against the us-east serving pool with default drain_timeout (30s).
2) Simulate a mix of short chat and long-stream requests at 60% of typical sustained throughput.
3) Observe that when nodes begin connection drain, in-flight requests to drained nodes are reset and the API gateway retries, amplifying load to remaining nodes.
4) Understood sequence: drain -> connection resets -> gateway retries -> remaining runtimes hit sudden concurrency -> some runtimes evict workers / hit alloc pressure -> 502/503s escalate.
logs: 2026-03-10T03:14:23Z runtime-3 stderr: kvcache: failed to allocate buffer: out of memory
2026-03-10T03:14:24Z apigw: 502 from runtime-3 for request id=rq_89f0 - connection reset during body streaming
2026-03-10T03:20:01Z autoscaler: scale_up event triggered by elevated_reqs - launching 2 nodes (warmup)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: improper drain behavior caused abrupt connection closes rather than graceful handoff; gateway retries amplified remaining capacity and caused runtime worker eviction/ooms.
Checked autoscaler timeline: scale-up lag was ~3 minutes; warm-up CPU/memory usage peaked as newly launched nodes ramped, but too late to absorb burst.
Observed increased KV cache miss rate during window which magnified per-request compute as caching benefits were reduced.
Network telemetry shows SYN/FIN patterns consistent with in-flight connection termination rather than graceful keepalive shutdown.
root_cause: Combination of aggressive connection drain policy during rolling deploy (drain_timeout too low) and unforgiving gateway retry amplification. Drained nodes cut live streaming connections instead of allowing graceful completion; gateway retried immediately, pushing more load onto remaining runtimes that then experienced memory pressure and partial OOMs.
workaround: Rolled back the rolling deploy controller to use extended drain_timeout for streaming-heavy pools (increase to 120s) and temporarily disabled immediate gateway retry for specific routes to reduce amplification.
resolution_plan: 1) Short term: Revert to previous deploy config and set drain_timeout=120s for prod-us-east streaming-capable pools.
2) Mid term: Implement streaming-aware drain that marks nodes as 'no-new-streams' before connection deadline to allow existing streaming clients to finish without hard resets.
3) Add a backoff window in API gateway retries for 5xx during deploy windows to avoid amplification.
4) Tune autoscaler warmup policies to reduce scale-up lag for heavy workloads and pre-warm cache for new nodes.
5) Create a runbook for deploys that adapt drain_timeout by workload type and register mandatory canary traffic windows.
postmortem_actions: Documented deploy drain change in runbook
PR opened to add streaming-aware drain logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1292
Dashboard alert created for rapid-5xx-change with auto-annotation of deploy events
resolution: Mitigation applied: rollback and adjusted drain_timeout. Immediate customer impact reduced to baseline within 9 minutes of mitigation steps. Longer-term fixes scheduled and tracked under INT-2109 and infra PRs.
